terms.meaning: Seven: China, Nepal, Bhutan (north), Myanmar, Bangladesh (east), Pakistan (north-west), Sri Lanka (south).
The part of Kashmir Pakistani forces seized in 1948.
The 3440 km India-China border, named after Sir McMahon of the British government.
Signed by Nehru and Chinese Prime Minister Chou-En-Lai in 1954.
South Asian Association for Regional Co-operation, begun in 1985.

items.name: Problems between India and Pakistan
items.formula: Kashmir, military attacks, terrorism, water dispute, protection of minorities, trade.
items.example: Kashmir has been the main obstacle since 1947.

items.name: Wars with Pakistan
items.example: Pakistan gave 2,700 sq km of Jammu and Kashmir land to China.

items.name: Shimla Agreement (1972)
items.formula: After the 1971 war, signed under Indira Gandhi: solve all issues, including Kashmir, by peaceful talks.

items.name: Lahore Bus Yatra and after
items.formula: In 1999 Vajpayee started the Amritsar-Lahore bus; the Agra summit failed.

items.name: Tibet
items.formula: China took military control of Tibet in 1950; India sheltered more than 80,000 Tibetans with the Dalai Lama.
items.example: Tibetan settlements in Karnataka: Bailukuppe (Mysore) and Mundagod.

items.name: The 1962 war
items.formula: China attacked from the eastern borders to Ladakh (Aksai Chin) and still holds the land it took.
items.example: China also claims 90,000 sq km in Arunachal Pradesh.

items.name: Nepal
items.formula: A landlocked country with an open border; ties rest on the 1950 Friendship and Peace Agreement.
items.example: Under the 1971 trade treaty, Nepal's goods enter India tax-free.

items.name: Bhutan
items.formula: By the 1949 agreement India won't interfere inside Bhutan, which seeks India's help in foreign affairs.
items.example: India helped Bhutan join the UN and gave aid from 1961 to 1981.

items.name: Sri Lanka
items.formula: Ashoka sent Buddhist missionaries. Tamils sought a separate state; India sent the IPKF in 1988.
items.example: The LTTE killed Rajiv Gandhi on 21 May 1991; Katchatheevu island was settled in 1974-76.

items.name: Bangladesh
items.formula: Once East Pakistan; Sheikh Mujibur Rehaman's Awami League led its struggle; independent in 1971 with India's help.
items.example: In 1972 the two signed a 25-year friendship treaty; Chakma refugees remain an issue.

items.name: SAARC members
items.formula: India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Afghanistan.
items.example: Afghanistan joined as the eighth member in 2007.

items.name: Aims of SAARC
items.formula: Mutual trust, welfare of South Asian people, and economic, cultural and scientific co-operation.
items.example: India launched a satellite for SAARC members to share academic information.

mistakes.text: SAARC began with seven members in 1985; Afghanistan is the eighth. Myanmar and China are neighbours but not members.
The Shimla Agreement was 1972, after the 1971 war; the Panchasheela was with China in 1954.
The 1999 war with Pakistan is the Kargil war; the 1962 war was with China.
